classification_statement: A learned surrogate (DERIVED physical geometry and field features -> collisionless test-particle wall-loss probability per axial cell) of the SCREENING_L1A_FIELD_TEST_PARTICLE_WALL_LOSS dataset produced by modern/experiments/orbit_wall_loss_geometry_screening_v1. Every prediction inherits that label: it is a surrogate of a SCREENING dataset on L1a linear-vacuum fields (not P2-qualified), never physical-orbit evidence, never a plasma or thruster-performance model. v2 tests ONE change against v1 on the identical frozen roles: whether a Gaussian process (or a per-stage-count GP mixture) on realised geometry / field descriptors, instead of the raw design selectors whose step discontinuities defeated v1, interpolates the screening dataset to v1's predeclared accuracy with calibrated uncertainty; and whether a tree ensemble (which represents steps natively) does better. It does not test physics.

claim_boundary.statement: Surrogate of a SCREENING dataset; not physical-orbit evidence; not a performance model. The targets are orbit-integration outcome counts on L1a screening fields; the surrogate reproduces those counts' probabilities within a declared accuracy inside a declared interpolation scope. Nothing here validates the orbit model, the field model, the mirror picture or any thruster figure of merit. The v1-vs-v2 comparison compares two surrogates of the same screening dataset; it says nothing about physics.
usable_as: if accepted: a design-dependent wall-loss input for an MDO v2 that carries the SCREENING label and the interpolation scope (predictor.json marked usable_as_mdo_v2_input_with_screening_label)
a sensitivity report of which DERIVED geometry / field features drive the screening wall-loss probability
a paired comparison (same 16 assessment designs, same 10 extrapolation designs) of raw-design-parameter inputs (v1) against derived physical features (v2)
a learning curve quantifying what a v3 with more designs could expect
forbidden_readings: that P(wall) predicted here is the wall-loss probability of a real thruster or of a self-consistent plasma
that the surrogate is accurate outside the interpolation scope (the extrapolation assessment is reported, its gate may fail)
that passing the interpolation gates validates the orbit or field models
that the ARD length-scales, permutation importances or tree feature importances are physical sensitivities rather than sensitivities of the screening dataset
that a v2 improvement over v1 is evidence about the physics rather than about the input representation of a surrogate
claim_boundary.prior_surrogate_failures_disclosure: Nineteen earlier surrogate campaigns (l0_surrogate v1-v9, l1a_field_surrogate v1-v10) failed their predeclared gates or were invalidated (lack of physically varying data, non-group-valid conformal ranks, a tautological target). wall_loss_geometry_surrogate_v1 (the first on physically varying data) was recorded rejected_surrogate: pooled RMSE 0.056 > 0.05, floor-corrected cell RMSE 0.128 > 0.05, best-baseline ratio 1.11 < 2 (coverage 0.90 passed). Its permutation importance placed almost all signal on the step-discontinuous design selectors (stage_count_selector, exit_length_fraction), which a stationary GP on the raw selectors cannot represent. v2 changes exactly the input representation (and adds a tree baseline) and keeps v1's roles and gates verbatim so the result is directly comparable.

authority.template_campaigns: modern/experiments/wall_loss_geometry_surrogate_v1 (lifecycle, gates, partition, predictor contract; its data.py / models.py / predictor.py / experiment.py are imported and hash-bound), modern/experiments/mdo_l0_campaign_v1 (experiment_runtime lifecycle, shakedown gate)
authority.prior_surrogate_protocol_lineage: modern/experiments/l0_surrogate_v2 (role partition, single-use assessment), l0_surrogate_v5 (method-selection / calibration / assessment roles), l0_surrogate_v9/POSTHOC_AUDIT.md (tautology rejection), wall_loss_geometry_surrogate_v1 (rejected; diagnosis motivating v2)

dataset.git_binding_rule: the dataset and manifest working-tree bytes must hash to dataset_file_sha256 / manifest_file_sha256, their Git blob ids at screening_result_commit must equal dataset_git_blob / manifest_git_blob, the manifest entry for the dataset must carry the same byte hash, and screening_result_commit must be an ancestor of HEAD
dataset.label_rule: P(wall) = termination_counts.wall_hit / trial_count of the accepted-2N case (pooled, 512 launches) and per_cell[accepted-2N][cell].wall_hit.successes / trials (128 launches per cell); P(reflect) = termination_counts.reflected / trial_count; the dataset's stored probabilities must equal these ratios exactly

v1_binding.binding_rule: every listed v1 file must hash to the declared sha256 and byte count, its Git blob at result_commit must equal git_blob and the working-tree blob, result_commit must be an ancestor of HEAD, v1's partitions.json must reproduce from v1's declared partition rule on the same dataset, and v1's campaign-result.json must carry recorded_status / recorded_selected_candidate
v1_binding.comparison_use: v1's per-design assessment predictions (assessment.json) are read ONLY in the assessment stage, after v2's own single-use assessment labels, to produce the reported (non-gated) paired v1-vs-v2 comparison on the identical 16 assessment and 10 extrapolation designs

inputs.statement: The inputs are DERIVED physical geometry and L1a field features: deterministic arithmetic functions of each design's committed screening-dataset row (geometry, field.sweep_qois, launch_design.cell_to_field), which itself copies the committed L1a geometry sweep v2 results. No feature is fitted, tuned, scaled by data statistics or learned; the extraction code features.py is bound by hash in the code contract. The eleven raw design selectors of v1 are deliberately NOT inputs.
inputs.provenance_source: features.FEATURE_TABLE (name, unit, kind, provenance formula) and features.EXCLUDED_RECORDED_QUANTITIES; published as artifacts/features.json
inputs.stage_count_representation: stage_count enters as the integer (3/4/5) AND as three one-hot columns for the GP candidates; the per-stage-count mixture candidate routes on stage_count
inputs.known_discontinuities: none by construction: the steps of the design -> geometry map (stage count, polarity, exit suppression) are realised categorical / one-hot features or realised lengths, not continuous selectors
inputs.degeneracy_check: continuous features must take >= 8 distinct values across the 96 designs; discrete features (stage_count, the three one-hots, first_polarity) must have >= 2 levels each with >= 5 designs; the 96 feature tuples must be distinct; fails closed otherwise
inputs.normalisation: affine unit box fitted on the FIT role only (minimum / span per feature); assessment and extrapolation inputs may fall outside [0, 1]; the mixture's per-stage-count GPs share this single unit box

outputs.pooled_identity: p_wall_pooled equals the mean of the four cell probabilities exactly (equal trials per cell); it is fitted as its own output and the identity is verified on the data, not exploited by the model
outputs.no_tautology_statement: Each target is a count of orbit terminations produced by orbit_mc v1.7 relativistic-Boris integration in an L1a re-solved field of the design; no algebraic expression of the derived features yields the count (the map passes through a PCG field solve and an event-driven ODE integration with 512 launches). The per-cell cusp / null distances describe where a cell sits in the field, not how many orbits terminated in it. The campaign verifies (a) the stored probabilities equal integer count ratios, (b) no target column equals an affine function of any single feature column, (c) a LEAVE-ONE-OUT ridge regression on the 31 features over the fit role does not reproduce the held-out fit-role targets to better than the binomial floor (leave-one-out rather than v1's in-sample fit because 32 coefficients on 50 designs overfit in-sample without any tautology; an algebraic target would still be reproduced out of sample).

known_noise.model: binomial: each label is a sample proportion s/n with n = trials
known_noise.direct_transform_noise_variance: p_tilde (1 - p_tilde) / n with p_tilde = (s + 1) / (n + 2) (Laplace-smoothed so that s = 0 or s = n never yields zero noise)
known_noise.logit_transform: empirical logit y = log((s + 0.5) / (n - s + 0.5)) with noise variance 1 / (s + 0.5) + 1 / (n - s + 0.5) (Haldane-Anscombe); the inverse map is the logistic function applied to the latent mean and to the interval endpoints
known_noise.prediction_time_observation_noise: added unscaled to the calibrated latent variance: logit scope 1 / (n p_hat (1 - p_hat)) with p_hat = clip(sigmoid(m), 0.5 / (n + 1), (n + 0.5) / (n + 1)); direct scope p_hat (1 - p_hat) / n with p_hat = clip(m, 1 / (n + 2), (n + 1) / (n + 2)); the observation interval is the interval an independent n-launch replicate should fall in

outputs.noise_floor_rule: the binomial floor of an assessment set is sqrt(mean over its labels of p (1 - p) / n) with the observed p; floor-corrected RMSE = sqrt(max(RMSE^2 - floor^2, 0)); both raw and floor-corrected RMSE are recorded for every output and scope

partition.rng: random.Random(int.from_bytes(sha256(namespace + ':' + str(seed) + ':' + stratum)[:8], 'big')).shuffle(sorted case ids of the stratum); roles are then assigned in order fit, method-selection, calibration, assessment with the declared counts (v1's rule, verbatim)
partition.identity_rule: the recomputed partition must equal v1's committed partitions.json (semantic sha256 v1_binding.partitions_semantic_sha256) exactly: same seed namespace, seed, strata, counts and therefore the same case ids in every role; v2's partitions.json is byte-identical to v1's

extrapolation_cluster.rule: the ceil(0.10 * 96) = 10 designs with the largest geometry.chamber_length_m (ties broken by case_id) form the EXTRAPOLATION hold-out; they take part in no other role and are never used for fitting, selection or calibration

role_semantics.fit: the only labels any model may be fitted on (also the pool of the learning curve)
role_semantics.method-selection: labels used once to choose among the declared candidates, the ridge penalty and the tree hyperparameters, and to score the learning curve; never used for fitting the final model
role_semantics.calibration: labels used once to fit the single variance scale of the 90 % intervals; never used for fitting or selection
role_semantics.assessment: SINGLE-USE: opened once in the assessment stage after the model, the selection and the calibration are frozen and written; scores the interpolation-scope gates and the paired v1 comparison
role_semantics.extrapolation: SINGLE-USE: opened once in the assessment stage; scores the extrapolation-scope report and its paired v1 comparison

partition.frozen_record: partitions.json is written by prepare (case ids per role, sha256 of the sorted id list per role), must equal v1's partitions.json, and its semantic hash is bound in authorities.json; execute and the prebundle stage recompute the partition from the protocol and refuse on any difference
partition.label_access_records: every extraction of labels from the dataset is preceded by an ExperimentRuntime before_expensive(kind='label') access record naming the role, so the bundle proves the assessment and extrapolation labels were first read in the assessment stage

candidates.selection_criterion: mean over the five gated outputs of the raw P-unit RMSE on the method-selection role; lowest wins; ties broken by declared order

definitions.botorch-stgp-logit: (a) BoTorch SingleTaskGP with train_Yvar (fixed binomial noise), covar_module = get_covar_module_with_dim_scaled_prior(ard_num_dims=31, use_rbf_kernel=False) (Matern-5/2 ARD with the dimension-scaled LogNormal length-scale prior), ConstantMean, Standardize outcome transform, fit_gpytorch_mll (scipy L-BFGS-B), torch float64 on cpu with 8 threads, torch.manual_seed(0) before each fit; on the empirical logit of each output, one model per output, on the 31 derived features (stage count as integer + one-hot)
definitions.botorch-stgp-direct: the same SingleTaskGP on the direct proportion with Laplace-smoothed binomial variance
definitions.stage-mixture-stgp-logit: (b) per-stage-count GP mixture: for every realised stage count with >= 8 fit-role designs (rule declared here; the fit role has 13 / 29 / 8 designs for 3 / 4 / 5 stages, so all three counts qualify) one botorch-stgp-logit model is fitted on that count's fit designs only, all sharing the same prior family, transform and fit-role unit box; a design is routed to the GP of its realised stage_count; a stage count with < 8 fit designs is served by the all-count botorch-stgp-logit model (declared fallback, also fitted); the predictor contract encodes the routing as an explicit dispatch rule per output

mixture_rule.one_hot_fallback_note: had any stage count fewer than 8 fit designs, that count would be served by the all-count GP whose inputs already include the stage-count one-hot, i.e. the 'stage count one-hot' alternative

baselines.global-mean: fit-role mean of each output (P units)
baselines.knn-3: unweighted mean of the 3 nearest fit-role designs in the fit-role unit box (Euclidean over the 31 features; ties by case id)
baselines.ridge: ridge regression on the unit-box features plus intercept (P units); penalty chosen on the method-selection role from [0.0001, 0.001, 0.01, 0.1, 1.0] by the mean-RMSE criterion
baselines.gbt: gradient-boosted regression trees (scikit-learn GradientBoostingRegressor, squared error, subsample 1.0, random_state 0, deterministic) on the unit-box features, one ensemble per output in P units, predictions clipped to [0, 1]; hyperparameters chosen on the method-selection role from max_depth in {1, 2, 3} x n_estimators in {100, 300} at learning_rate 0.05 by the mean-RMSE criterion; included because trees represent steps natively - if the tree baseline beats the GP, that is itself the finding
baselines.best_baseline_rule: for the 2x gate the best baseline is the one with the LOWEST raw pooled-P RMSE on the assessment role itself (conservative against the surrogate)

calibration.method: cft_revival.surrogates.VarianceCalibrator.fit on the 50 standardised residuals (five gated outputs x ten calibration designs) in the selected candidate's working space, where the standardising variance is latent posterior variance + prediction-time observation noise; the resulting single variance_scale multiplies the total predictive variance of every output (including p_reflect_pooled)
calibration.rank_rule: order statistic ceil((n + 1) * 0.9) - 1 of the sorted |residual| / sd (n = 50 -> the 46th of 50)

determinism.rule: after the final model is written, every fitted component is refitted from scratch in-process on the same fit rows; working-space latent means and variances at the assessment and extrapolation inputs must agree within 1e-9 (absolute) and hyperparameters within 1e-9 relative; bit-exactness is recorded

interpolation_rmse_pooled.statement: raw RMSE of p_wall_pooled over the 16 assessment designs <= 0.05

interpolation_rmse_cells.statement: floor-corrected RMSE over the 64 assessment cell predictions (four cells x 16 designs) <= 0.05; the raw RMSE is reported beside it because the 128-launch cell labels carry a binomial floor of about 0.035

beats_best_baseline_2x.statement: raw pooled-P RMSE of the best baseline on the assessment role >= 2.0 x the surrogate's raw pooled-P RMSE (the tree baseline is one of the baselines)

coverage_90.statement: empirical coverage of the calibrated 90 % observation intervals over the 80 assessment predictions (five gated outputs x 16 designs) lies in [0.80, 0.97]

no_tautology.statement: the three no-tautology checks of outputs.no_tautology_statement pass

determinism_replay.statement: candidates.determinism rule holds for the selected model

dataset_binding.statement: dataset.git_binding_rule holds, v1_binding.binding_rule holds, the derived features pass the degeneracy check and the dataset's stored probabilities equal integer count ratios

partition_frozen_single_use.statement: the recomputed partition equals partitions.json, v1's partitions.json and the frozen authority hash; role sets are disjoint with the declared counts; the label access records show assessment and extrapolation labels first read in the assessment stage after the predictor artifact was written

predictor_contract_replay.statement: the dependency-light predictor (predictor.py on predictor.json, including the mixture dispatch) reproduces the fitted model's working-space latent mean and variance at every assessment and extrapolation input within 1e-9

code_contract.statement: source hash, package versions and python minor version equal the preregistered authority

extrapolation_rmse_pooled.statement: raw RMSE of p_wall_pooled over the 10 extrapolation designs <= 0.10 (may fail; reported honestly)

extrapolation_rmse_cells.statement: floor-corrected RMSE over the 40 extrapolation cell predictions <= 0.10

extrapolation_coverage_90.statement: coverage of the 50 extrapolation intervals in [0.80, 0.97]

beats_best_baseline_2x_cells.statement: best-baseline raw cell RMSE >= 2.0 x surrogate raw cell RMSE

reflect_output.statement: p_reflect_pooled RMSE and coverage on both scopes are reported without a gate

v1_comparison.statement: paired comparison against v1's committed assessment predictions on the IDENTICAL 16 assessment designs (and the identical 10 extrapolation designs): per-output RMSE v2 vs v1, pooled and cell RMSE differences, number of designs on which |v2 error| < |v1 error| for p_wall_pooled, and whether v2 improves pooled RMSE; also the tree baseline vs the selected GP; reported, never gated

learning_curve.statement: the selected candidate refitted on nested seeded fit-role subsets of size 20 / 30 / 40 / 50 (three seeds; size 50 = the whole fit role), scored on the method-selection role; a log-log slope and the extrapolated number of fit designs needed for pooled RMSE 0.05 are reported to quantify what a v3 would need; reported, never gated

gates.acceptance: all binding gates pass -> accepted_surrogate and predictor.json is marked usable_as_mdo_v2_input_with_screening_label; otherwise the campaign is recorded as rejected_surrogate with every metric published, predictor.json is marked not_usable_as_mdo_v2_input_rejected_surrogate, and campaign-result.json records why it failed and what v3 would need (from the learning curve and the tree-vs-GP comparison)

sensitivity.ard_length_scales: per output and per mixture part, in fit-role unit-box coordinates; a large length-scale means the output is insensitive to that feature

permutation_importance.metric: increase of the raw P-unit RMSE on the fit role when one feature column is permuted across the fit designs, averaged over repeats; per output and averaged over the five gated outputs

sensitivity.tree_feature_importance: scikit-learn impurity-based feature_importances_ of the selected gbt baseline, per output and averaged; reported beside the GP sensitivities

learning_curve.subset_rule: random.Random(sha256('wall-loss-geometry-surrogate-v2:learning-curve:' + candidate + ':' + str(seed))) shuffles the sorted fit-role case ids; the subset of size n is the first n ids (nested across sizes); size 50 is the whole fit role
learning_curve.extrapolation_rule: least-squares fit of log(mean pooled RMSE) = a + b log(n) over the four sizes; if b < 0 the designs needed for pooled RMSE 0.05 are exp((log 0.05 - a) / b); otherwise 'more designs of the same kind are not predicted to reach the gate'

active_learning_addon.note: v1's add-on is not repeated; the learning curve replaces it as the reported development analysis

shakedown.purpose: Exercise the complete production path (dataset binding, v1 binding, feature derivation, partition, every candidate, baselines incl. gbt, selection, calibration, predictor export with dispatch, determinism replay, sensitivity, learning curve, assessment metrics, v1 comparison, gates, publication through the shared ExperimentRuntime into a temporary root, validate_bundle) on the REAL dataset with a DIFFERENT partition seed namespace before the preregistration freeze. Gates are informational. Because the dataset is finite and fixed, the shakedown necessarily reads every label; the evidentiary information barrier is procedural: protocol, gates and candidates are frozen by hash before prepare, the shakedown record is bound into the authorities, and any protocol edit after the shakedown invalidates it.
prepare_requires: protocol_semantic_sha256 equals the current protocol hash
source_sha256 and package versions equal the current code contract
shakedown partition differs from the evidentiary (= v1) partition (different role assignment)
runtime terminal state accepted_result and bundle validated
all candidates fitted, a selection recorded, predictor replay passed

artifacts: artifacts/features.json (feature manifest with provenance; per-design feature table)
artifacts/baselines.json (incl. gbt grid scores and feature importances)
artifacts/assessment.json (per-design predictions, truths, intervals for both scopes)
artifacts/v1-comparison.json (paired v1 vs v2 on the identical designs)
artifacts/campaign-result.json (status, mdo_v2_input_status, rejection reasons and v3 requirements when rejected)
